sections.head: The things people wonder before they ring
sections.body: Someone else quoted less. That quote was made up before anyone had seen your house — a number off the top of someone's head with no site visit is not a fixed price, it's a starting point that grows once the ceiling is open. Dan quotes after a visit. The fixed price is real. On scope: the written report names what can honestly wait, not just what's billable. If something doesn't need doing now, that goes in writing too. On mess: every job is tidied up properly when it's finished.

sections.head: Right for you if your house is older and the electrics have been nagging at you
sections.body: Most of the work is in older semis — pre-war and post-war houses that came with vague survey warnings about dated electrics. The kind where the surveyor wrote 'dated electrics, recommend further investigation' and everyone filed it away under 'sort later.' If that note has been sitting on your desk, or you've noticed a socket that looks wrong, or the lights flicker and don't resolve themselves, that's what the Home Safety Check is designed for. You find out exactly what's there. In writing. Before anything is spent on the fix.

about.head: Why the written report tells you what can wait — not just what needs doing
about.body:
Old houses round here hide things. Live wires behind bathroom tiles. Fuse boards that should have been replaced years ago, still running a family home. Sockets sitting brown and warm behind a piece of furniture. The surveyor caught a glimpse and wrote 'dated electrics' in the report. Then life happened.

When I started doing this, I noticed something. Homeowners weren't just worried about the job — they were worried about me. Was I making work? Was the scope invented? Was there a cheaper way I wasn't mentioning because it didn't suit me?

So I changed what I write up after a visit. The report doesn't just list what's dangerous and what needs doing. It lists what can honestly wait a few years. In plain English, with photographs, on paper you can show someone else. It takes longer to put together. But it's the reason people trust the quote — because a report that tells you what you don't need to spend money on right now is clearly not a report designed to inflate your bill.

I'm based in Ossett. I cover Wakefield, Horbury, Dewsbury and out to about 25 minutes. I photograph everything. I agree a fixed price in writing before work starts. I turn up when I said I would. None of that should be unusual in this trade. Apparently, it still is.

sections.head: You already know something isn't right. You just don't know how wrong.
sections.body:
The survey said 'dated electrics' and you told yourself you'd deal with it. That was months ago. Now there's a socket you've been ignoring — brown around the edges, or warm to the touch. Maybe it's lights in one room that flicker and don't resolve themselves. Maybe it's a smell you can't fully locate and keep telling yourself isn't there.

The fear underneath all of this is specific: the house catching fire. Especially at night. Especially near where the kids sleep. You're not catastrophising — older houses do have wiring that fails. The question is whether yours does, and how badly.

Right now you don't know. That's the part that keeps you awake. The Home Safety Check exists to answer that question — not to sell you a job that isn't there, but to tell you exactly what is.

sections.head: The Home Safety Check — what it is, what it costs, and what you get
sections.body:
The Home Safety Check is an electrical installation condition report carried out by Dan at your property. The price is £165, fixed and agreed in writing in advance.

On the day: Dan visits, photographs the wiring and the fuse board, checks any switches and sockets of concern, and looks at whatever your original survey flagged.

What you receive: a plain-English written report in three clear sections. What is dangerous and needs immediate attention. What is wrong and should be fixed. And the part nobody else round here includes — what can honestly wait a few years. Every finding is specific. Photographs are included. The report is certified.

The price is £165 and it does not change on the day.

If you go on to book a Full House Rewire or Full House Rewire with EV Charger Ready within 60 days of the report being issued, the £165 is deducted from the job price.

sections.head: The questions worth asking before you book
sections.body:
Is there a cheaper option? Probably. A quote over the phone, no site visit, a number made up before anyone has looked at your house. That price tends to grow once the work is under way and the full picture appears. Dan quotes after seeing what's actually there. The fixed price is real, and it is agreed in writing before work starts.

Will the scope be invented? The written report includes what can honestly wait. If a circuit is fine, that goes in writing. If a fault is minor and can sit for a couple of years, that goes in writing too. You can take the report to any other Part P registered electrician and ask them to check it.

How much disruption? The Home Safety Check is a visit and a report — no building work that day. If a full rewire follows, the job is planned around your house, the place is left tidy at the end of each day, and the work is done in days rather than weeks.
sections.cta: Book your Home Safety Check — Dan visits and writes up exactly what he finds for £165

sections.head: If the report misses something dangerous, Dan returns and reinspects at no charge
sections.body:
On the Home Safety Check: if the written report misses a dangerous or potentially dangerous fault that a subsequent inspection by any other Part P registered electrician identifies within 90 days, Dan returns to the property and reinspects at no charge, then issues a corrected written report. This is a promise of his own action — returning and reinspecting — not a guarantee of any particular outcome.

On a Full House Rewire or Full House Rewire with EV Charger Ready: the 6-year workmanship guarantee is written onto the quote as a named, signed term. Any notifiable work that does not pass its Building Regulations certification inspection is redone by Dan at no extra charge until it is certified and lodged.

sections.head: What comes after the report: the Full House Rewire
sections.body:
If the Home Safety Check confirms the house needs rewiring, two options are on the table — both at a fixed price agreed in writing before work starts.

The Full House Rewire is £4,500. The fuse board is replaced, circuits are run properly, all notifiable work is certified and lodged, and the 6-year workmanship guarantee is written onto the quote.

The Full House Rewire with EV Charger Ready is £5,450. The EV charger is fitted in the same week as the rewire — one booking, one week of disruption, wiring and charging sorted in a single job.

Book either rewire within 60 days of your written Home Safety Check report and the £165 is deducted from the total.
